audit_objective: Determine whether '1-day move was ...' or 'move_1d' entered canonical training vs evaluation runs.

training_leakage_details.content: pretest["earnings_transcript"] = pretest["company_name"].fillna("") + " reported earnings on " + pretest["date"].astype(str) + ". 1-day move was " + pretest["move_1d"].astype(str)
syn_text = f"{co_name} reported earnings on {date_str}. 1-day move was {move_1d}"

training_input_leakage.leaked_string_format: pretest["company_name"] + " reported earnings on " + pretest["date"] + ". 1-day move was " + pretest["move_1d"]
training_input_leakage.mechanics: The target label is defined as (move_1d <= -4.69%). Concatenating the exact continuous realization of move_1d into the input string provided the model with the ground truth label during training and pre-2022 validation.
training_input_leakage.evidence_validation_note: Validation AUROC during training reached 0.9998 - 1.0000 across all seeds because the model trivially extracted the move_1d string.

evaluation_input_leakage.note: During all clean out-of-sample inference (2022-2025), input text NEVER contained move_1d, future returns, or label-derived quantities.

conclusions.root_cause_of_oos_collapse: Because models were trained with '1-day move was ...' in the text, but evaluated on clean text without that phrase, the models suffered extreme test-time distribution shift. Lacking the outcome tokens, the model's test-time discriminative ability collapsed to random chance (AUROC ~ 0.50), and predicted probabilities collapsed toward the empirical base rate (~0.18).
conclusions.formal_classification: INVALID_HISTORICAL_TRAINING: Phase-11 replication and Phase-16 initial deterministic control adapters were trained on outcome-leaked text strings and must be formally classified as compromised training artifacts.
